collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older; a single popup, no choice)

collection.description: Swinging in a hammock, a villager takes stock of life and decides that, so far, it has been pretty good.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: (name1) is lying in (his/her) hammock in the late afternoon, swinging gently, looking up through the palm leaves at bits of blue sky, and taking a sort of inventory. Some things went the way (he/she) planned. Most didn't. A few went much better. There are a couple of mistakes (he/she) still winces about, a few people (he/she) misses, a few dreams that drifted off somewhere, and a startling number of very good meals. (He/she) has been lucky and unlucky in roughly equal amounts, which seems fair. (He/she) is not famous, not rich, not the best at anything, and not finished yet. A breeze comes through. A bird lands on the hammock rope, looks at (him/her), and leaves again. (name1) laughs out loud at nothing in particular and decides that, so far, all things considered, it's been pretty good.
